fields.v: Wang, Y., Jiang, Z., Wang, R., Gong, N. Z. (2026). Package Hallucination Attacks on Coding Agents through Prompt Injection in Rule Files. arXiv:2610.09264v1 [cs.CR], 7 Oct 2026
Preprint (arXiv)
Duke University, USA (all four authors)

Proposes an approach (package hallucination attack and PackHallu, an evolutionary optimizer of malicious prompts injected into rule files); secondary: evaluates (attack success across 3 benchmarks, 8 agent frameworks, 13 LLMs; 5 detectors)
PackHallu (attack framework; no version). Target artefact: coding rule files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules) shared via open-source platforms and marketplaces

Not a development approach. Artefacts: benign coding rule file with an injected malicious prompt (default at the beginning); attacker-controlled malicious package (interface-compatible, suffix _hl) on a local PyPI mirror

Attack: seed prompt -> evolutionary loop (surrogate agent simulated by an LLM produces trajectory; trajectory-level signal scores occurrences of malicious package; attack LLM self-attributed critique -> strategy -> rewrite of offspring; top-k selection) for R rounds -> best prompt injected into rule file -> victim agent loads rule file and generates code
None (victim agents run in autonomous mode with manual confirmation disabled)
Single artefact (rule/context file) as attack vector, loaded by real agent frameworks; no specification
Not classifiable (rule-file security attack, no specification); authors do not use SDD terms
New code (file-level code generation from scratch: BigCodeBench, DS-1000) and existing code base (repository-level multi-file refactoring: RefactorBench)

BigCodeBench 981 tasks (5 packages, 80% victim / 20% surrogate), DS-1000 772 tasks (4 packages), RefactorBench (5 packages; count in appendix Table 17); 10 victim packages; detection benchmark 200 rule files (100 benign, 100 malicious)
Python; data science and general third-party packages (pandas, numpy, matplotlib, scipy, seaborn; kombu, twisted, urllib3, asgiref, werkzeug); software supply-chain security
N/A (no human participants)

Automatic: import detection in generated code, execution with print-based malicious behaviour from local PyPI mirror, attention extraction, detectors' outputs. Manual (presumably): categorization of 87 Claude Code trajectories (procedure Not stated)

Criterion: SASR/DASR on BigCodeBench (attack effectiveness, i.e., vulnerability of agent). (1) PackHallu + OpenHands + 5 backbones (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, Qwen3-Coder-30B, Devstral-Small-2-24B, GLM4.7-Flash-30B, Gemma4-31B), same surrogate and victim: avg SASR 79.29%, DASR 67.68% (per package SASR 70.02-86.19%). Attack works. (2) Baselines on same settings: Combined Attack avg 14.99/11.35; Repeat, GCG, ObliInjection lower; TAP strongest baseline (e.g., Qwen3-Coder-30B Pandas 34.62/26.92 vs PackHallu 98.72/89.74). Do not work / partly (TAP). (3) Transfer to other backbones on OpenHands (12 LLMs incl. GPT-5.5, GPT-5.3-Codex, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Llama-4-Maverick): >90% SASR on >=3 of 5 packages for 8 of 12; Qwen2.5-Coder-7B only 22.73-50.00% SASR. Works. (4) Transfer to other frameworks with Qwen3-Coder-30B (OpenCode, Aider, Pi, Cline, Kilo Code): avg SASR 71.55%, DASR 62.99%. Works. (5) Claude Code + Claude Sonnet 4.6: SASR 31.03-58.95%, DASR 31.03-57.89%. Partly (most resistant). (6) Cursor + Auto: SASR 69.35-98.00%; Cursor + Composer 2.5: 81.40-95.65%; OpenCode + DeepSeek-V4-Flash: 75.32-93.94%. Works. (7) Dataset transfer: DS-1000 SASR 53.33/DASR 45.00; RefactorBench 18.60/16.28. Partly / does not work (repository level). Ablations: injection at beginning best (avg SASR 82.63 vs 74.03 middle, 77.29 end); 4 paraphrased initializations 98.00±2.09 SASR; removing trajectory-level signal drops SASR 83.87->56.99. Cost verdict: not measured

Tasks: BigCodeBench (main), DS-1000, RefactorBench adapted by package. Configurations: PackHallu vs 5 prompt-injection baselines (Combined, Repeat, GCG and ObliInjection with white-box advantage, TAP with same surrogate); 8 frameworks x 13 LLMs for transfer. Held constant: rule-file loading per framework recommendation, autonomous mode, injection position, local PyPI mirror, single prompt optimized on numpy pair reused for all packages. Acceptance: execution and import checks. Repetitions: Not stated (single runs apparently; std only for initialization ablation). Human intervention: none (autonomous)

PackHallu outperforms all baselines on all packages and victim agents: avg 79.29/67.68 vs best simple baseline Combined 14.99/11.35 (5.29x SASR, 5.96x DASR). More capable backbones more vulnerable (r=0.785 for SASR vs capability); no relation across frameworks (r=-0.186). Popular packages harder to attack (median r=-0.69). No significance tests. Detectors: ProtectAI-DeBERTa FNR 100%; PromptGuard 46%/5% FPR; DataSentinel 49%/16%; PromptArmor 20%/34%; PIShield 21%/11%

Distinguished attacks clearly (large gaps). Repeatability: initialization ablation shows stability; repetitions per configuration not stated; no statistical tests. Authors state no limitations of the comparison method
No limitations section. Gaps: robust defences for the collaborative rule-file pipeline; existing detectors inadequate; attack weaker at repository level (RefactorBench)
